statement: Checking that a citation exists isn't enough. You also have to check that the source actually says what it's cited for.
Any AI-assisted literature review should state which AI tools were used and for which steps.
Given its current error rates, AI should not be used to search the literature at all.
Citation errors made by AI are no worse than the citation errors humans have always made.
An AI that accurately summarizes manipulated sources is a bigger threat than an AI that makes things up.
Letting AI read and summarize papers for us will weaken the deep reading skills that scientists need.
We shouldn't say a report was written with AI unless the authors admit it. Clues like oaicite tags in links aren't proof.
Continuing to use AI for literature searches will lead to papers reusing the same citations over and over again.
